headline: Build your 'Second Me' with a practical framework for encoding yourself into an AI agent
summary: Learn a week-by-week framework to train an AI agent on your unique thinking, decisions, and tacit knowledge, going beyond simple chatbots.
details: Andrej Karpathy's "second self" concept, an AI trained on your personal patterns, goes beyond a chatbot to mirror your thinking. This framework aims to capture not just explicit knowledge but also tacit understanding.

The article outlines a practical, week-by-week system combining behavioral recording, think-aloud extraction, and chain-of-thought distillation. It focuses on building an agent that thinks and defaults like you.
A functional "Second Me" has four layers: declared knowledge (wiki), tacit knowledge (behavioral), decision-making models, and reasoning chains. The framework primarily addresses the latter three.
Weeks 1-2 focus on creating a raw reasoning corpus using the Think-Aloud Protocol. Narrate your thoughts while performing tasks, capturing spontaneous insights and tacit knowledge.
Identify high-value recording triggers like complex problem-solving, difficult decisions, or learning new skills. Use low-friction tools for recording and transcribe everything.
Mark transcripts for "gold" patterns: unconscious first steps, critical questions, and moments of tacit knowledge escaping. This annotation is crucial for turning raw data into training signals.
Weeks 3-4 involve building structured skill manifests. Instead of procedures, these are decision-making models that explain how you decide, not just what you do.
This involves pulling relevant recordings, identifying unconscious first steps, mapping decision trees, and surfacing edge cases. The goal is to capture the unique aspects of your expertise.
caption:
Ever wished for an AI that truly thinks like you? This framework shows how to build your "Second Me" by encoding your unique decision patterns and tacit knowledge into an AI agent.

Andrej Karpathy's "second self" concept, an AI trained on your personal patterns, goes beyond a chatbot to mirror your thinking. This framework aims to capture not just explicit knowledge but also tacit understanding.

The article outlines a practical, week-by-week system combining behavioral recording, think-aloud extraction, and chain-of-thought distillation. It focuses on building an agent that thinks and defaults like you.

A functional "Second Me" has four layers: declared knowledge (wiki), tacit knowledge (behavioral), decision-making models, and reasoning chains. The framework primarily addresses the latter three.

Weeks 1-2 focus on creating a raw reasoning corpus using the Think-Aloud Protocol. Narrate your thoughts while performing tasks, capturing spontaneous insights and tacit knowledge.

Identify high-value recording triggers like complex problem-solving, difficult decisions, or learning new skills. Use low-friction tools for recording and transcribe everything.

Mark transcripts for "gold" patterns: unconscious first steps, critical questions, and moments of tacit knowledge escaping. This annotation is crucial for turning raw data into training signals.

Weeks 3-4 involve building structured skill manifests. Instead of procedures, these are decision-making models that explain how you decide, not just what you do.

This involves pulling relevant recordings, identifying unconscious first steps, mapping decision trees, and surfacing edge cases. The goal is to capture the unique aspects of your expertise.
